attempts.raw_response: The tiger had come upon them quite by accident, having been driven from its usual hunting grounds by the recent heavy rains that had flooded the lower reaches of the jungle. It was a young male, they agreed, probably three years old and still foolish enough to wander so close to human habitation. Sir Morland produced a flask of brandy from his tent and poured generous measures all round, for the night had turned chill and the excitement had left them all with shaken nerves. His brother Charles remarked that it was a mercy the beast had taken fright so readily, for a cornered tiger of mature years might have made a very different story of it. They discussed the incident at some length, speculating upon where the creature might have come from and whither it might now be bound. Eventually, as the first grey light of dawn began to soften the darkness, the party retired once more to their beds, though few of them slept soundly for the remainder of the night.

pair.human_continuation:
A Thrilling Story

One evening, in Assam, a young Englishman was driving along a lonely
jungle road. He wished to visit a neighbouring Saheb; and though his
servants had warned him that tigers had been frequently seen on that
particular road, he had laughed at their fears and told them that
the only tiger to be feared was a "man-eater", and that there were no
"man-eating" tigers about that district. As usual in the mofussil of
India, he was going out to dine and sleep, and his bearer had put up
his clothes and his suit case was stowed into the dog-cart.

The road was a good one and considerably wide, for it was the main
thoroughfare in the district and along it tea, jute and all other
agricultural products were transported to the river for export to other
districts of India and also to Europe.
pair.prefix:
The terrified tiger gave a
mighty roar, turned tail and fled.

The camp was aroused. Everyone shouted and rushed out into the night,
armed with some weapon or other. Sir M. related to his brother guns
what had happened and they all enjoyed a good laugh and rather envied
him for the fine sight he had of such a superb specimen of the kings
of the jungle.
